name: Forehand block
summary: Use the opponent's speed and spin against them with a short, firm stroke close to the table.

name: Backhand block
summary: The safest answer to a fast topspin on the backhand: angle the bat, meet the ball early, let it rebound.

name: Forehand loop against topspin
summary: Topspin against topspin: a more forward swing that adds speed and spin to an incoming topspin ball.

name: Counter-loop
summary: Loop the opponent's loop back from mid-distance, taking it after the bounce peak with a full body swing.

name: Backhand topspin
summary: A spinny backhand opening and rally shot driven by forearm and wrist from in front of the body.

name: Forehand flick
summary: Attack a short ball over the table with a quick forearm and wrist action.

name: Backhand flick
summary: Attack a short serve or push with the backhand over the table. The banana flick adds sidespin at higher levels.

name: Short touch
summary: Drop a short ball back short so it would bounce twice: soft hands, early contact, tiny stroke.

name: Smash
summary: Finish a high ball with a fast, flat hit at the top of the bounce.

name: Forehand chop
summary: A defensive stroke from far back: brush down and forward under a topspin ball to send heavy backspin.

name: Backhand chop
summary: The backhand defensive chop: a long down-and-forward stroke that returns topspin with backspin.

name: Lob
summary: A high, deep, spinny return from far back when the opponent attacks. Keeps you in the point.

name: Forehand pendulum serve
summary: The most common serve: backspin, sidespin, no-spin or topspin from the same motion.

name: Reverse pendulum serve
summary: The pendulum swing reversed, giving sidespin the other way. Great for variation.

name: Tomahawk serve
summary: A forehand serve with the bat tip pointing up, swinging across the body for strong sidespin.

name: Backhand serve
summary: A compact serve from in front of the body, easy to learn and good for a fast start to the rally.

name: Attacking long serves
summary: Punish any serve that comes long: step back a touch, read the spin and attack with topspin.

name: Reading spin
summary: Tell backspin, sidespin, topspin and no-spin apart from the opponent's bat path and contact.

name: Cross-over step
summary: A big step across to cover a wide forehand when a side step is too slow.

name: Pivot
summary: Step around the backhand corner to play a forehand from there.

name: In-and-out footwork
summary: Move in for short balls and back out for long ones without losing balance.

name: Placement
summary: Use the wide forehand, wide backhand and the playing elbow on purpose.

name: Changing pace and spin
summary: Mix fast and slow, heavy and light, so the opponent never settles.

name: Playing against styles
summary: Plans for choppers, blockers, pips, loopers and penholders.

name: Agility
summary: Quick first steps and fast changes of direction.

name: Core strength
summary: A strong middle that links legs to arm and protects the back.

name: Shoulder and wrist care
summary: Small exercises that keep the playing arm healthy for years.

name: Handling nerves
summary: Play your game when the score is close and it matters.
